searched: Read in full: LAW_SYSTEM.md, IMPROVE_SYSTEM.md, REGRESSION_SYSTEM.md, CONTEXT_SYSTEM.md, hooks/system-health-check.py, hooks/skip-flag-ledger.py, _design-system/CONTRADICTIONS.md, _plans/SELF_AUDIT_2026-07-25.md, _design-system/DESIGN_GOVERNANCE_AUDIT_2026-07-10.md, _plans/RETRO_2026-07-06.md (partially, via head/wc), CLAUDE.md (project, from system context), REMOVED.md, hooks/SHELVED.txt. Ran counts: 134 global hooks (.py/.sh), 30 project hooks, 19 global skills, 116 memory files (1915-word index, 652K on disk), word counts on every doctrine file (LAW/IMPROVE/REGRESSION/CONTEXT/LOOP/REPORT/MODEL_ROUTING/FABLE_DNA/PREFERENCES = 7965 words total), both CLAUDE.md files (9284 words), _design-system (130 files, 410091 words, dominated by a 280992-word _pending-migration.md and LOCKFILE.md at 19637 words / SOURCE.md at 13258 words), _rules (25101 words). Grepped, across _backend-system, _docs, _rules, _design-system, CLAUDE.md, ~/.claude/*.md and both hooks directories, for: gate-mute/re-scope thresholds, doc-size ceilings, ceiling-names-its-floor generalization beyond design, rule-retirement language, rule-count ceilings, and a cost-must-beat-mistakes test -- first with a broad pattern (caught mostly noise from _backend-system research prose, discarded) then narrowed to the actual law/doctrine/audit files. Inspected hooks/_retired (12 files, zero README, zero doctrine mention, not scanned by system-health-check.py's non-recursive listdir) and hooks/SHELVED.txt (26 lines, a wiring-manifest convention, distinct from a retirement policy). Checked how many project hooks cite LOCKFILE.md/SOURCE.md directly (2 of 30) to corroborate the design-governance audit's claim that those canonical files are enforced by a hand-copied, drifted regex subset rather than a live reference.

findings.title: A gate skip-flagged past a set rate must be re-scoped or retired, not left as a live-but-ignored law
findings.principle: Any gate whose skip-flag fires more than 10 times in a rolling 7 days (or more than 3 times for a single-purpose gate that is not a shared family) is automatically flagged at the next SessionStart as REQUIRES-DECISION: the owner picks narrow-scope, merge-into-family, or retire within 7 days, and until that decision is made the gate's deny message states out loud that it is under review. A gate that keeps firing and keeps getting skipped is not enforcing anything; it is a toll the owner pays to keep working, and the system currently has no mechanism that turns that toll into a forcing question.
findings.why: LAW_SYSTEM.md section 2 says a misfiring gate must be TUNED, never silently disabled, because 'a disabled gate is a lie: everyone believes the law is enforced and nobody is enforcing it.' But a gate that is skip-flagged 72 times in 6 days is functionally disabled by a thousand tiny cuts instead of one big one, and the same lie results: system-health-check.py reports it as wired and enforcing, when in practice it enforces almost nothing. Nothing currently distinguishes 'skipped twice for real exceptions' from 'skipped every single time it fires.'
findings.local_evidence: _plans/SELF_AUDIT_2026-07-25.md section 2: the 7-member mockup gate family was skip-flagged 72 times in 6 days (28+14+13+9+8+4+4+... across mockup-approved/preflight/content/lang-icon/grounding/real-base/english); finish-autonomously-skip.flag alone was used 40 times in 6 days, 'the single most-muted gate.' Both are explicitly logged as 'OWNER CALL, parked' with no automatic trigger -- the audit had to notice this by hand-reading a 745-line log, and next week's self-audit will have to notice it by hand again.
findings.absence_proof: grep -in 'muted.*re-scope|re-scope.*gate|skip.*threshold|mute.*gate|delete.*gate|too often.*gate' across LAW_SYSTEM.md, IMPROVE_SYSTEM.md, REGRESSION_SYSTEM.md, both self-audits, and CLAUDE.md returned only the self-audit's own prose describing the 40x number, never a rule defining a threshold or an automatic consequence.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: LAW_SYSTEM.md section 2 has 'a misfiring gate gets TUNED, never silently disabled' and skip-flag-ledger.py logs every use for visibility, but neither ties a NUMBER to an automatic escalation. Visibility without a threshold is a report, not a law.
findings.where_it_should_live: LAW_SYSTEM.md section 2 (tiers) or a new section 7, plus a small hook reading skip-flag-ledger.log on SessionStart
findings.enforcement: gate: skip-flag-ledger.py already has every row it needs; add a weekly aggregator (could live in system-health-check.py as an 8th invariant) that counts flag-uses per flag-name in the last 7 days and injects a REQUIRES-DECISION line into SessionStart context when a threshold is crossed

findings.title: No cap on how many independent gates may deny the same action serially before they must be merged
findings.principle: When more than 3 independently-registered PreToolUse hooks can each individually deny the same tool call (same event, overlapping matcher), they must be consolidated into one aggregator hook that returns a single combined manifest of every unmet requirement in one deny, before a 4th sibling gate is added to that action. Serial one-at-a-time denials on the same edit are what turn a legitimate law into something worth mass skip-flagging.
findings.why: One deny per turn costs one round trip and reads as one obstacle to route around (skip-flag once). Thirteen independent denies on the same Write, discovered one at a time as each is silenced or satisfied, cost thirteen round trips and read as an adversarial gauntlet, not a law -- this is a direct, measured contributor to the mockup family's 72x/6-day skip rate in the previous finding. LAW_SYSTEM.md section 6.2 already states the target ('one gate per failure class, extend the existing gate rather than wiring a second overlapping one') but nothing checks whether that target is being met in practice, and no owner or session revisits an old family once it exists to ask whether it grew past the target.
findings.local_evidence: _design-system/DESIGN_GOVERNANCE_AUDIT_2026-07-10.md, Part 2 finding 1 (ranked #1 of the whole audit): '13+ independently-registered PreToolUse gates each deny one at a time on a mockup Write (live-tested: two probes, one message each).' The fix proposed there (a mockup-preflight aggregator) was itself only a recommendation from a one-time audit, not a standing rule that would catch the next family before it reaches 13.
findings.absence_proof: grep -in 'one gate per|consolidat.*gate|aggregator.*gate|serial.*gate|gate.*count' across LAW_SYSTEM.md and the two audits found LAW_SYSTEM's aspirational sentence (section 6.2) and the one-time audit finding, but no numeric cap and no recurring check.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: LAW_SYSTEM.md section 6.2 states the goal in prose ('one gate per failure class'); it is not measured or enforced anywhere, and the one place it was measured (the 2026-07-10 audit) found it already broken by a factor of 13x with no re-check since.
findings.where_it_should_live: LAW_SYSTEM.md section 6 (laws about the law system), enforced via an addition to system-health-check.py that groups hooks by declared matcher+event and flags any group above the threshold
findings.enforcement: gate: a system-health-check.py invariant that parses each hook's registered matcher from settings.json/settings.local.json, groups by (event, matcher-pattern), and flags any group with more than 3 members as 'consolidation candidate'

findings.title: No policy for retiring a gate independent of supersession; the existing _retired/ folder has no criteria, no tombstone, and is invisible to the health check
findings.principle: A gate may be moved to hooks/_retired/ only with a one-line dated entry in a RETIRED_GATES.md ledger naming the gate, the date, the failure class it used to catch, and why that class is judged dead (superseded by a different gate, the underlying surface was deleted, or it has not fired a true positive in 90+ days). system-health-check.py must scan hooks/_retired/ and flag any file there with no matching ledger entry as an unaccounted-for retirement.
findings.why: LAW_SYSTEM.md section 3.6 defines retirement only for the SUPERSESSION case ('a law superseded by a newer dated owner decision moves to the graveyard... with a tombstone line'). It says nothing about a gate that simply stops earning its keep with no replacement decision. In that gap, retirement has already been happening by hand with zero paper trail, which is exactly the 'deletion without a tombstone... zombie rules resurrect' failure the same section warns against for the covered case.
findings.local_evidence: hooks/_retired/ contains 12 files (coder-marker-subagentstop.py, english-mockup-gate.py, mockup-contract-hue-gate.sh, mockup-dataviz-ink-gate.sh, mockup-english-lucide-gate.sh, mockup-gate.py.bak-before-harden, muted-color-gate-v2.sh, no-caps-gate.py, no-decorative-separator.py, no-emdash-gate.py, no-verbose-ui-copy.py, readback-contract-gate.py) with no README and zero mentions in LAW_SYSTEM.md, REGRESSION_SYSTEM.md, or any doctrine file found by grep. system-health-check.py's check_hook_wiring() only calls os.listdir(hooks_dir) non-recursively on the top-level hooks/ dir, so files inside _retired/ are never inspected at all -- a retired no-caps-gate.py could be silently un-retired (copied back up a level) and the health check would treat it exactly like any other orphan, with no memory that it was once deliberately killed.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rin 'retir|tombstone|graveyard|supersede' on LAW_SYSTEM.md found only the supersession clause (section 3.6) and the exists-check pointer (section 6.3); a separate find for a RETIRED_GATES.md, hooks/_retired/README, or any doctrine reference to the _retired directory by name returned nothing.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: the supersession-tombstone rule (LAW_SYSTEM.md 3.6) covers the case where a newer decision replaces an older one; it does not cover a gate retired for disuse/decay with no successor, which is the actual shape of everything sitting in hooks/_retired/ today.
findings.where_it_should_live: LAW_SYSTEM.md section 3 (lifecycle) as step 6b, plus system-health-check.py invariant 1 extended to scan _retired/
findings.enforcement: gate: system-health-check.py addition, self-testable (block case: a file in _retired/ with no ledger line; pass case: one with a line)

findings.title: No size ceiling on a 'read before every edit' canonical law file, so the two biggest ones are self-admittedly unread
findings.principle: Any file marked as canonical/must-read-before-editing (the role LOCKFILE.md and SOURCE.md hold for design work) may not exceed roughly 3,000 words / ~20KB. Past that size the file must fork into a thin always-loaded index (the frozen literals only) plus linked detail sections loaded on demand, because a file nobody actually re-opens before a small edit is not canon, it is an archive that happens to be cited as canon.
findings.why: The entire point of a T0 doctrine file per LAW_SYSTEM.md section 2 is that it 'shapes behavior when read.' A file too large to plausibly be re-read before a routine edit cannot do that job no matter how correct its content is, and the project's own workaround (pasting a 10-item cheat sheet into CLAUDE.md) is an admission that the canonical file failed at its one job, not a fix to why it failed.
findings.local_evidence: _design-system/LOCKFILE.md measures 19,637 words (this session's own wc -w) and SOURCE.md 13,258 words. The project CLAUDE.md itself states the consequence in its own voice: 'SOURCE.md + LOCKFILE hold the full system, but they're 80KB+ and I don't re-read them before a small edit, so I drift.' The fix chosen was a duplicate 10-rule summary block inside CLAUDE.md (the taste-rules section) rather than shrinking LOCKFILE/SOURCE -- which is itself a second source of truth that can (and per CONTRADICTIONS.md and DESIGN_GOVERNANCE_AUDIT, has) drifted from the original.
findings.absence_proof: grep -in 'too big|doc size|word limit|nobody reads|max.*words|size limit|too large' across LAW_SYSTEM.md, CONTEXT_SYSTEM.md, CLAUDE.md, and _design-system/CONSOLIDATION_2026-07-12.md found only the CLAUDE.md line quoted above describing the problem, no rule addressing it.
findings.existing_coverage: none as a rule; CONTEXT_SYSTEM.md section 1 defines a BASELINE/WORKING-SET/SEDIMENT cost model for the whole context window and names 'law compression' as one of the only fixes for baseline bloat, but never sets a per-file threshold that would trigger that compression.
findings.where_it_should_live: CONTEXT_SYSTEM.md section 6 (baseline diet) as a concrete threshold, cross-referenced from LAW_SYSTEM.md section 4 (placement law)
findings.enforcement: checklist / doc-only in the first pass (a wc -w check is trivial to add as a lint, but deciding what to split out of a 19k-word file is a judgment call the owner should make once)

findings.title: No standing, automated reconciliation between canonical values in doctrine and the literal values hardcoded inside a gate script
findings.principle: Every gate that hardcodes a literal allow-list mirroring a canonical doc value (hex codes, retired token names, durations) must ship with a CI check that diffs its literal set against the doc's own value table, run on every push touching either file, not rediscovered by an occasional hand-audit whose own method can silently be wrong for a week.
findings.why: A gate that blocks a value the doc actually allows produces a false positive that trains the operator to skip-flag past the gate (feeding finding gate-mute-forces-rescope); a gate that fails to list a value the doc retired produces a false negative that lets drift back in silently. Both directions were found live in this estate, and the mechanism that found them (a human audit) had itself been wrong the previous week without anyone noticing.
findings.local_evidence: _plans/SELF_AUDIT_2026-07-25.md section 7a: the 2026-07-18 audit text-grepped check.py and reported '10 missing hexes / 4 missing RETIRED_TOKENS,' both wrong, because the grep counted commented-out and prose hexes as live set members. The 2026-07-25 pass switched to an AST-parsed ground truth and found 25 LOCKFILE hexes absent from ALLOWED_HEX (16 genuine false positives that block legitimate tokens) and 7 genuine RETIRED_TOKENS gaps (s-amber, the s-love family, four s-atm-* variants). This has now happened as a one-off manual pass twice, a week apart, with a wrong answer the first time.
findings.absence_proof: grep for 'reconcil|ast-pars|diff.*lockfile|CI.*token' across LAW_SYSTEM.md and REGRESSION_SYSTEM.md found no rule; the reconciliation exists only as a step inside the weekly self-audit checklist (SELF_AUDIT step 7), which is a task-list item, not a standing gate or test.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: the weekly self-audit (an owner-sanctioned but manual cadence) performs this reconciliation once a week by hand; it is not automated, not run on the actual edit that introduces drift, and its own method changed without a rule forcing the change (the AST-fix was one engineer's improvement, not a mandated correction procedure).
findings.where_it_should_live: a script alongside .claude/skills/solen-drift-check/scripts/check.py, wired into the same CI path as scripts/check-invariants.mjs (already exists per RETRO_2026-07-06.md)
findings.enforcement: gate: a CI job (extending .github/workflows/invariants.yml, which already exists per the retro) that fails a push touching LOCKFILE.md or check.py if the two value sets diverge

findings.title: No test that a new law/gate/doctrine layer must be provably cheaper than the mistakes it prevents before it is written
findings.principle: Before authoring a new doctrine file, gate family, or research-to-law layer (the shape _backend-system's research/ folder is currently in, 15 files with no LAW.md yet), the proposal must name: (a) the specific, counted incidents it would have prevented in the last 90 days, (b) the ongoing per-session cost it adds (injection bytes, extra tool calls, extra doc a human must read), and (c) a one-line comparison showing (a) outweighs (b). A law layer that cannot point to a counted incident is premature machinery, not prevention.
findings.why: This project runs about 28 salons, pre-launch, roughly 29 test files, no real customers. Big-company governance (a frozen backend LAW.md with the ceremony of a security review board) is the kind of premature machinery the project's own CLAUDE.md warns against for PRODUCT code ('adopting big-company machinery early is itself a failure mode'), but that warning has never been applied reflexively to the AGENT-GOVERNANCE layer itself, which has grown to 134 global hooks, 30 project hooks, and roughly 460,000 words of design-system-adjacent doctrine for a single operator working with AI agents. Nothing forces a 'is this worth what it costs' question before the next doctrine file is written.
findings.local_evidence: _backend-system/README.md (per the orchestrator's own briefing) promises LAW.md/RATIONALE.md/AUDIT.md/QUESTIONS.md at its root and none exist, while 15 research files and 8 audit files already do -- research is being produced faster than law is being frozen, with no gate asking whether freezing more law is the right next move versus, say, nothing (at 28 salons, most of the 15 backend topics researched, e.g. rate-limiting or observability at scale, may not need a frozen law yet at all). Separately, CONTEXT_SYSTEM.md's own numbers (64% of spend at >150k context) show the estate is already expensive to carry; no matching number exists for 'and here is what that expense bought us in prevented incidents.'
findings.absence_proof: grep -in 'cheaper than|cost of the system|worth the cost|pays for itself|ROI' across LAW_SYSTEM.md, IMPROVE_SYSTEM.md, and REGRESSION_SYSTEM.md returned nothing.
findings.existing_coverage: none for the meta layer; CLAUDE.md's scale-discipline framing exists but is scoped to product/backend decisions (e.g. when to add sharding, when to add a queue), never turned inward on the governance system that makes those decisions.
findings.where_it_should_live: LAW_SYSTEM.md section 3 (lifecycle), as a precondition before step 2 (ledger entry) for anything bigger than a single gate
findings.enforcement: checklist (a one-paragraph justification required in the same commit/turn that introduces a new doctrine file or gate family; not machine-checkable, but a Stop-gate could at least require the paragraph to exist in the PR/commit message)

findings.title: No ceiling on total rule/gate count and no 'one-in-one-out' consolidation budget
findings.principle: The global hooks directory tracks its own count on every SessionStart; crossing 150 wired hooks (currently 134) triggers a mandatory consolidation review before the 151st is added: at least one existing hook in the same family must be merged, narrowed, or retired for every net-new hook past that line, and the review's outcome is logged the same way a lessons-ledger entry is.
findings.why: Every hook is a permanent tax paid on every relevant tool call, forever, by every future session, whether or not it still catches anything. There is currently no counter-pressure against growth: /harden's whole workflow (CLAUDE.md rule, ~/.claude system) is optimized to ADD a gate for every new recurring mistake, and nothing in that workflow ever asks whether an existing gate should die to pay for the new one. The 13-gates-on-one-mockup-Write finding (a separate entry in this report) is the visible symptom of exactly this: growth with no matching contraction.
findings.local_evidence: 134 top-level .py/.sh files in ~/.claude/hooks (measured this session), 30 more in the project's .claude/hooks, plus 19 skills and a 116-file, 652KB memory directory. LAW_SYSTEM.md section 6.2 asks for 'one gate per failure class' but has no counter or threshold; the design-governance audit found the mockup family alone already at 13x that target with no automatic re-check since 2026-07-10.
findings.absence_proof: grep -in 'too many rules|rule count|rule sprawl|law sprawl|how many (rules|laws|gates)' across LAW_SYSTEM.md and IMPROVE_SYSTEM.md returned nothing.
findings.existing_coverage: none; the closest neighbor is CONTEXT_SYSTEM.md's injection-BYTE diet (each hook's payload must be small and deduped), which controls per-hook cost but never the COUNT of hooks.
findings.where_it_should_live: LAW_SYSTEM.md section 6, enforced by system-health-check.py (it already counts hooks implicitly via check_hook_wiring; add a raw count + threshold)
findings.enforcement: gate: system-health-check.py invariant, informational at first crossing (nudge), blocking a NEW hook file's Write past the threshold without a matching retirement named in the same turn

findings.title: The skip-flag ledger's rotation silently destroys the week-over-week trend that is the audit's most useful signal, and nothing preserves it first
findings.principle: Before skip-flag-ledger.py's trim (LEDGER_MAX_LINES=800, keeps the last LEDGER_KEEP_LINES=500) discards any lines, it must append a one-line rollup (date range, total count, top-5 flags by count) to a separate, never-trimmed skip-flag-history.log, so a rotation is a compression of raw lines into a summary, never a deletion of the aggregate.
findings.why: The self-audit that measures gate health depends on comparing this week's skip counts to last week's; that comparison is the whole point of catching a gate whose muting is accelerating rather than steady. A silent line-count-based rotation with no pre-trim snapshot means that comparison randomly stops being possible the moment the log crosses 800 lines, which is exactly what happened.
findings.local_evidence: _plans/SELF_AUDIT_2026-07-25.md section 2: 'The log was rotated/started on 2026-07-19, so there is no prior-week baseline this pass and week-over-week deltas (the 2026-07-18 audit's most useful output) cannot be computed.' The same file's own closing 'Observations for the doctrine' section 3 names this exact gap and proposes the fix ('the audit should snapshot weekly totals into its own report') but that proposal has not been turned into a rule or code change, so the next rotation will destroy the trend again.
findings.absence_proof: grep for 'rollup|history.log|pre-trim|snapshot.*ledger' in skip-flag-ledger.py and LAW_SYSTEM.md found only the trim_if_needed() function itself (which discards, not summarizes) and the self-audit's own diagnosis, no code or rule implementing the fix it names.
findings.existing_coverage: none as a rule; the gap was self-diagnosed by the project's own audit process but sits as an 'observation,' not a law, so it is not binding on the next session that touches the ledger.
findings.where_it_should_live: skip-flag-ledger.py's trim_if_needed(), documented in REGRESSION_SYSTEM.md or LAW_SYSTEM.md wherever ledger conventions are defined
findings.enforcement: gate: a two-line code change to trim_if_needed(), self-tested with a synthetic 801-line ledger asserting the history file gained exactly one rollup line

findings.title: A design-law contradiction that gets fixed does not automatically enter the same anti-recurrence ledger a code bug does, so fixed design contradictions have already regressed silently
findings.principle: Any entry in _design-system/CONTRADICTIONS.md (or an equivalent design-token audit) that is marked resolved must also get a _rules/LESSONS_LEARNED.md entry with a File(s) line naming the token/component, so lessons-ledger-inject.py's PreToolUse advisory fires the next time someone edits that file, exactly as it would for a code bug. A 'this contradiction is fixed' note that lives only in a design audit doc is invisible to the one mechanism (REGRESSION_SYSTEM's injector) proven to actually stop repeats.
findings.why: REGRESSION_SYSTEM.md's entire thesis is that the FIX of a bug lands in git but the KNOWLEDGE of it dies with the session unless it is bound to the file at edit time; that thesis applies exactly as hard to a design-token drift as to a select-star leak, but the design side runs its own separate audit trail (CONTRADICTIONS.md, DRIFT_LEDGER, TASTE_LOG) that was never required to feed the one ledger the injector actually reads.
findings.local_evidence: _design-system/CONTRADICTIONS.md's own header note (added 2026-07-12, a month after the file was marked EXECUTED): 'the 2026-07-12 consolidation census (A4) found 6 of the classes marked done here have since REGRESSED (hairline, sunken, radius, press-scale, disabled-opacity, dead-hover).' Six fixed classes came back with nobody's edit-time tooling warning them, because REGRESSION_SYSTEM.md's injector only reads _rules/LESSONS_LEARNED.md (hardcoded path per REGRESSION_SYSTEM.md section 2), and CONTRADICTIONS.md is a different file.
findings.absence_proof: grep -in 'contradictions.md' _rules/LESSONS_LEARNED.md-style cross-references and REGRESSION_SYSTEM.md found the ledger's hardcoded single-source design (section 2: 'This is the SOLE ledger the injector reads') with no bridge rule requiring a resolved CONTRADICTIONS.md item to also become a LESSONS_LEARNED.md entry.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: REGRESSION_SYSTEM.md fully solves this problem for anything that DOES get ledgered; the gap is that design-contradiction fixes are not required to go through that path, and a separate audit trail (CONTRADICTIONS/DRIFT_LEDGER/TASTE_LOG) was allowed to grow as a parallel, weaker memory system for the same class of knowledge.
findings.where_it_should_live: REGRESSION_SYSTEM.md section 2 (ledger) as an explicit bridge rule, or a one-line addition to whatever process marks a CONTRADICTIONS.md item done
findings.enforcement: checklist (marking a contradiction item as done requires the LESSONS_LEARNED line in the same turn); could be gated by extending pre-commit-graveyard.sh-style logic to also check CONTRADICTIONS.md edits

findings.title: Nothing forces the author of a new doctrine file to decide, at write time, whether it needs a T1 injector -- the gap is only found later by audit
findings.principle: Every new file placed under _design-system/ (or any project doctrine directory) that states a rule the owner expects to be followed must, in the same commit, either be wired into an existing injector's keyword/path list or carry an explicit one-line 'PROSE-ONLY, no injector: <reason>' note at its top. A doctrine file with neither is not a deliberate choice, it is an oversight waiting to be found by the next audit.
findings.why: LAW_SYSTEM.md section 2 already defines the T0/T1/T2/T3 ladder and states plainly that T0-only ('shapes behavior when read') is the weakest tier; what it does not do is force anyone to consciously pick a tier when a new file is created, so the default outcome is T0-and-forgotten, discovered only when an audit goes looking.
findings.local_evidence: _design-system/DESIGN_GOVERNANCE_AUDIT_2026-07-10.md, Part 3 finding 3, called out by the auditing agent itself as the HEADLINE finding: 'TASTE_LOG.md is WRITE-ONLY: zero hook references (grep-proven)... this is the single biggest forgetting mechanism, per the agent's plain-language verdict.' The same audit's Part 1 finding 5 found SENIOR_SCORECARD.md and WORK_TYPES.md similarly uninjected and unwired into the design-verifier agent's own definition. Confirmed independently this session: only 2 of the project's 30 hooks reference LOCKFILE.md or SOURCE.md by name at all, for files that CLAUDE.md itself calls canonical.
findings.absence_proof: grep -in 'tier check|injector.*required|must wire|authoring.*checklist' in LAW_SYSTEM.md found only the tier DEFINITIONS (section 2), never a rule requiring a tier decision to be made and recorded when a file is created.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: the tier ladder itself is well specified; what is missing is the forcing function that makes picking a tier mandatory rather than optional, at the moment of creation rather than the moment of a future audit.
findings.where_it_should_live: LAW_SYSTEM.md section 3 (lifecycle), as a new step 1.5 between 'incident' and 'ledger'
findings.enforcement: checklist first (a line item in whatever process creates a new _design-system/*.md file); could graduate to a gate that gates a Write of a new top-level _design-system/*.md file requiring either a grep hit in a known injector script or the explicit PROSE-ONLY note

findings.title: No principle bounds how long it should take a second person (or a fresh, un-primed agent) to become safely productive in this estate
findings.principle: The estate must maintain one entry-point document, no longer than a 10-minute read, that names every doctrine file's purpose in one line and the exact order to read them in; and once a year (or whenever a second human operator is onboarded, whichever comes first) that document must be walked literally, cold, by a fresh session with no prior memory, timed, to prove the estate is still learnable in bounded time rather than only navigable by the person who built it.
findings.why: LAW_SYSTEM.md section 5's index is genuinely close to this, but it is written as AGENT session-routing ('a fresh session that wants the rule about X walks: index -> doctrine -> ledger'), not as a human or cold-agent ONBOARDING path with a time budget; nothing checks that the index is still true, still complete, or still fast to use as the estate keeps growing (134 hooks and climbing). A system built and understood by exactly one operator across many stateless sessions has an implicit single-point-of-failure: institutional knowledge that lives in the owner's head about WHY a given file exists, which files are stale, and which of two similarly-named files (CONTRADICTIONS.md vs CONSOLIDATION vs DRIFT_LEDGER vs TASTE_LOG) is authoritative today.
findings.local_evidence: no 'onboard' string anywhere in ~/.claude/*.md (grepped this session). The estate's own audits repeatedly find files that look authoritative but are stale or superseded and only get caught by a dedicated audit agent (DESIGN_GOVERNANCE_AUDIT's whole Part 1 is a list of exactly this: StatusPill documented but deleted, a stale hex two lines from its correction, TASTE_LOG entries reading '[RESOLVED: BLUE]' a month after being superseded by gray) -- evidence that even the CURRENT single operator's tooling struggles to keep the map accurate, which would only get harder for a second person with none of the tribal context.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: LAW_SYSTEM.md section 5's index is the closest artifact and does real work for agent sessions; it has never been tested as a human/cold-start onboarding path, has no time budget, and has no cadence for re-verifying it is still accurate.

findings.title: Memory hygiene runs on a vague 'monthly-ish' cadence with no size or count trigger, for a 116-file, 652KB memory directory
findings.principle: Run /consolidate-memory whenever the memory index (MEMORY.md) exceeds 2,000 words OR the memory directory exceeds 120 files, whichever comes first, not on a calendar guess. Re-check the trigger at every SessionStart alongside the existing system-health-check invariants, since the same hook already reads memory-index state (invariant 2) and can add a size/count check for near-zero extra cost.
findings.why: CONTEXT_SYSTEM.md itself identifies the memory index as part of the BASELINE cost paid on every single turn of every session ('the system prompt (both CLAUDE.md files ~47KB, memory index ~17KB...)'), and names /consolidate-memory as the fix, but ties it to a calendar guess ('Monthly-ish') rather than to the actual growth signal, so the trigger can silently slip for a stretch while the index keeps growing and every session keeps paying more baseline cost than the previous one.
findings.local_evidence: CONTEXT_SYSTEM.md section 6: 'Monthly-ish: /consolidate-memory (merge dupes, prune the 97-file index).' Measured this session: the memory directory now holds 116 files (up from the 97 the doctrine text still cites, meaning the doctrine's own reference number is already stale), a 1,915-word MEMORY.md index, and 652KB on disk.
findings.absence_proof: grep for 'memory.*trigger|memory.*threshold|consolidate.*when' in CONTEXT_SYSTEM.md found only the calendar-based 'Monthly-ish' line, no count- or size-based trigger.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: the fix (the skill) exists and is named; only the TRIGGER for running it is missing, and the doctrine's own cited file count (97) is already stale evidence that a calendar cadence is not actually being kept to.
findings.enforcement: gate: extend system-health-check.py invariant 2 (memory index) with a size/count threshold that surfaces alongside the existing unlinked/broken-link checks
